title: Enteral nutrition - child - managing problems

source.author: U.S. National Library of Medicine
source.license: Public domain (work of the US federal government)

body: Enteral feeding is a way to feed your child using a feeding tube. You will learn how to care for the tube and the skin, flush the tube, and set up the bolus or pump feedings. This article will help you manage minor problems that may occur with feedings.

Enteral feeding is a way to feed your child using a feeding tube. Enteral feedings will become easier for you to do with practice. Your health care provider will go over all of the steps you should follow to deliver the feedings.
You will learn how to care for the tube and the skin, flush the tube, and set up the bolus or pump feedings.
Sometimes a feeding does not go as planned, and you may have a minor problem. Your provider will go over all of the things that can happen and what you should do.
If your child is dehydrated, ask your provider about changing formula or adding additional water.
If your child is losing weight, ask your provider about changing formula or adding more feedings.
If your child's Corpak feeding tube falls out, contact your child's provider. Do not replace it yourself.
If your child has trouble breathing, call 911 or the local emergency number.

Updated by: Neil K. Kaneshiro, MD, MHA, Clinical Professor of Pediatrics, University of Washington School of Medicine, Seattle, WA. Also reviewed by David C. Dugdale, MD, Medical Director, Brenda Conaway, Editorial Director, and the A.D.A.M. Editorial team.
